feedback: No later iteration follows this one, so these requested changes can only apply if the design is re-run. The evidence: iteration 0 (baseline, 62.32) lost the line once per run with max_error 0.061 to 0.063 m. Iteration 1 widened the sensors to +/-0.045 m, which cut oval line losses from 1.05 to 0.55. Iteration 2 (mass 0.6 kg) cut oval losses further to 0.35, but s-bend and slalom still lost the line once (1.0). Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09 m) left those tracks at 1.0 losses with max_error 0.062 to 0.067 m, and oval progress at 0.121. Iteration 4 (+/-0.054 m span, scoring 67.90) cleared oval line losses (0.0) and lifted oval progress to 0.204, but s-bend and slalom still lost the line once, with max_error 0.0669 and 0.0648 m. The mass and track levers have now both been used without clearing those bends, so the sensor reach looks close to its limit for them. The Integrator has kept the iteration 4 geometry and controller, so the Builder's design races as tested. The points below apply only if a later design is raced: for an unseen track, keep the +/-0.054 m span with 0.027 m steps and sensor_size 0.012, because it removed oval line losses and kept max_error near 0.0625 m. Do not narrow wheel_track below 0.09 m or reduce mass below 0.6 kg, because those did not clear s-bend or slalom. If the unseen track shows line losses at max_error above 0.06 m, widen the outer sensors further (for example to +/-0.063 with 0.0315 m steps) before changing any other field.
requested_changes: If a later race shows a line loss with max_error at or above 0.06 m on a sharp bend: widen the outer sensors to x = +/-0.063 with 0.0315 m steps, keeping sensor_size 0.012. Iteration 4 showed that widening from +/-0.036 to +/-0.054 removed oval line losses and kept max_error near 0.0625 m.
Keep mass 0.6 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m: iterations 2 and 3 show that further mass or track narrowing did not clear the s-bend or slalom losses, and iteration 3 cut oval progress only slightly.
Keep sensor_size at 0.012 m: iteration 4 with that footprint was the best design measured, and no evidence supports changing it.
